jobs.title: Belonging Report
jobs.description: CREATING SPACE TO THRIVE: GONG’S YEAR OF BELONGING, GROWTH, AND REPRESENTATION Sandi Kochhar Chief People Officer Published on: May 28, 2025 Last modified on: August 19, 2026 Table of contents Building inclusive communities and allyship Looking ahead to FY26 Expand Win more with Gong Preparing form... Fostering a culture of belonging is more than just an intention — it’s a continuous commitment to creating an environment where every employee feels seen, heard, and valued. It’s one thing to build a successful business and create raving fans. But it’s equally important to create a company whose employees truly enjoy coming to work and showing up as their authentic selves. This year, my role as Chief People Officer feels just as important as it has ever felt. While broader conversations around diversity have shifted over time, at Gong, our commitment to inclusivity and belonging has never been about trends. It’s a reflection of the global, culturally diverse community that has been core to our success from the very beginning. At its core, Gong is a company dedicated to helping businesses grow, and we apply that same philosophy to our culture. We’re deeply committed to fostering an environment where every Gongster can grow, thrive, and reach their full potential. The evidence is clear: when people can bring their authentic selves to work, their potential is unlocked, and we all become stronger. As we look back on our last fiscal year, we’re proud to our progress. Building inclusive communities and allyship We conducted our first Blueprint Maturity Assessment with an external partner. We are proud to that Gong outpaced industry benchmarks in leadership engagement around belonging. We were also included in the top tier of companies that regularly conduct pay equity analyses and of companies that currently have a belonging strategy. A thriving workplace begins with a strong community that facilitates connection. To ensure everyone feels they belong at Gong, we focused last year on amplifying diverse voices, celebrating cultural moments, and fostering connections. We achieved that through Gong Circles, more than 30 employee-led events designed to build safe spaces and support networks. Our Allyship Listen & Learn Series also provided curated educational programming to support diverse communities, with dedicated events. The impact of these programs is felt and in our last engagement survey, 77% of our Gongstersd they feel like they “Belong at Gong.” To continue to hold ourselves accountable to fair and equitable pay, we partnered with an outside consultant to conduct our fifth annual pay equity analysis. Through these initiatives, we continue to build a more inclusive workplace where fairness, transparency, and accountability are paramount. Looking ahead to FY26 As we move into FY26, Gong will continue driving initiatives that promote belonging, inclusion, and equity across our organization. We will continue our focused support for underrepresented communities through our Circles, mentorship, and professional development opportunities. Our journey toward belonging is a daily and ongoing effort, and we’re excited to continue building a workplace where everyone can thrive. Together, we can create a culture that not only supports but actively celebrates diversity, equity, and inclusion. Check out our previous Belong@Gong annual updates: FY24 , FY23 , FY22 , FY21 . Checkout our Ireland pay gap report. Sandi Kochhar Chief People Officer Sandi Kochhar is the Chief People Officer at Gong, where she leverages over two decades of leadership in scaling teams and driving operational excellence. Before Gong, Sandi held executive roles at Ripple, AppDirect, Atlassian, and SuccessFactors, contributing to global expansions, M&A integrations, and IPO preparations. With a background as a Global Six Sigma Black Belt at Honeywell, she combines operational expertise with strategic leadership to support fast-growing tech companies.
